seo.title: Schengen Visa Guide for Indian Passport Holders | TripAgent
seo.description: The Schengen short-stay (Type C) visa for Indian passport holders: one visa for 29 European countries. Documents, biometrics, timelines, common rejection reasons, and how your advisor prepares and files it for you.

hero.lede: One short-stay visa, 29 European countries. For Indian passport holders it means biometrics, a careful file, and a peak-season appointment that can be hard to find. Here is how it works, and how we handle it for you.

what.heading: One visa, a whole continent.
what.lede: The Schengen area is a group of 29 European countries that share one visa. A short-stay (Type C) visa lets you travel for up to 90 days in any 180-day period for tourism: across all of them, on a single document. Indian passport holders need it; there is no visa-free or visa-on-arrival route for short tourist visits.
what.extraParagraph: You apply through the country that is your main destination, where you'll spend the most nights. If nights are equal, you apply through your country of first entry. Get this wrong and the application can be returned. We get it right.

what.heading: Count carefully.
what.lede: "90 days in any 180" is a rolling window, not a calendar year. On any given day, you can have spent no more than 90 of the previous 180 days inside Schengen. It is easy to miscount on a second trip in the same season. Your advisor keeps the count, so you never overstay by accident.

docs.heading: What goes in the file.

points.html: Passport valid at least three months beyond your intended departure, with two blank pages and issued within the last ten years.
Completed application form and a recent photograph to the exact Schengen specification.
Travel medical insurance covering at least €30,000, valid across the whole Schengen area for your dates.
Confirmed return flights and hotel bookings for the full itinerary: the proof the consulate wants to see.
Proof of funds: typically the last three to six months of bank statements, often with ITRs and Form 16 or salary slips.
A cover letter explaining the trip, plus employment or business proof and leave approval where relevant.
A day-by-day itinerary that matches your flights, hotels and the number of days requested.
For minors, parents or sponsors: additional consent, relationship and financial documents your advisor confirms.

docs.hedge: Exact requirements differ by the country you apply through and can change between seasons. Fees are as set by each consulate and its appointed visa centre. Your advisor confirms the current, precise checklist for your application before anything is submitted.

process.heading: Apply early. Especially in summer.
process.lede: You can apply up to six months before travel, and we recommend you do. In peak season, biometrics slots go early.

steps.heading: Choose the right country
steps.text: We identify the correct consulate to apply through based on your main destination, then route the application to its appointed visa centre (often VFS Global or BLS) in India.

steps.heading: Book the appointment
steps.text: Schengen biometrics are given in person. Appointments are scarce from roughly April to August: we secure the earliest viable slot and build the file around it.

steps.heading: Biometrics & submission
steps.text: Fingerprints and a photo are taken at the centre, valid for around 59 months so future Schengen trips may skip this step. The complete file is submitted on the same visit.

steps.heading: Processing & decision
steps.text: The standard processing time is around 15 calendar days, though it can extend to 45 days or more in busy periods or if extra documents are requested. We track it to passport return.

process.hedge: Validity and number of entries are set by the consulate: a first-time applicant often receives a visa matched to the trip dates, while frequent travellers with clean histories may receive longer multi-entry visas. Your advisor confirms what to expect for your profile.

pitfalls.heading: Why applications get refused.

what.heading: Every Indian traveller.
what.lede: India is not part of the US Visa Waiver Programme, so Indian passport holders need a visa for tourism or business. There is no ESTA route. The visa must be in hand before you board, and the interview is the heart of it.

docs.heading: What to bring.

points.html: A completed DS-160 online form and its confirmation page: accuracy here is essential.
Passport valid at least six months beyond your stay, plus any older passports showing travel history.
The visa fee paid (the MRV fee, as set by the US Department of State) and your interview and biometrics appointments.
A photograph to US specification, uploaded with the DS-160.
Proof of funds and ties to India: employment, business, property, family, to show you'll return.
Your travel purpose and rough plans; for business, an invitation or supporting letter.
For visiting family, the sponsor's details and relationship proof where relevant.
Any documents that support an honest, consistent account of the trip at interview.

docs.hedge: The visa is granted at the consular officer's discretion, based largely on the interview. Fees are as set by the US Department of State. Your advisor confirms the current process: including the two-step appointment system, before you apply.

process.heading: The wait is the whole problem.
process.lede: Interview slots are the bottleneck. At busy times the wait runs to many months. Start the moment a US trip is on the horizon.

steps.heading: File the DS-160
steps.text: We complete the online application accurately: the form the interview is built on, and pay the visa fee.

steps.heading: Book the appointments
steps.text: Most first-time applicants attend two: a biometrics visit at a Visa Application Centre and an interview at the consulate. We secure the earliest viable interview slot for your city.

steps.heading: The interview
steps.text: A short conversation with a consular officer about your trip, ties and intent. We prepare you so it's calm and consistent. Approval is at the officer's discretion.

steps.heading: Issuance & return
steps.text: On approval, the passport is sent for visa stamping and returned to you. We track it to delivery, and time the whole thing against your travel dates.

process.hedge: Some renewals may qualify for an interview waiver (the "dropbox") that skips the in-person interview: eligibility rules change, and your advisor confirms whether you qualify. Wait times differ greatly between cities and seasons; nothing here guarantees a slot or an outcome.

pitfalls.heading: Why it goes wrong.
pitfalls.lede: US refusals: often under section 214(b), usually come down to doubt about intent or an inconsistent file:

points.html: Failing to show strong ties to India, so the officer doubts you'll return.
An answer at interview that contradicts the DS-160 or the stated purpose.
Vague plans, or funds that don't match the trip you describe.
Leaving it too late, and losing the trip to interview waits, not to a refusal.

pitfalls.heading: A calm, clean interview.
pitfalls.lede: The interview rewards honesty and consistency:

points.html: Answer briefly and truthfully; your story should match your DS-160 exactly.
Be clear on your purpose, your funding and your reason to come home.
Carry supporting documents, but lead with a confident, simple account.
Above all, start early: the date you book is the date that decides the trip.

how.lede: Your advisor owns the US application from end to end. Where a renewal qualifies for an interview waiver, they pursue it, to spare you the consulate entirely.

We secure the earliest viable interview slot and prepare you for it.
We track the passport to return, or pursue an interview waiver where a renewal qualifies.

items.question: How long is the visa valid, and how long can I stay?
items.answer: For Indian applicants the B1/B2 is often issued for up to ten years, multiple-entry. That is the validity of the visa, not the length of each stay: how long you may remain each visit is set by the officer at the border, commonly up to six months.

items.question: Can I skip the interview on a renewal?
items.answer: Sometimes. Certain renewals qualify for an interview waiver: the "dropbox"that avoids an in-person interview. Eligibility rules change over time, so your advisor confirms whether your renewal qualifies before you apply.

items.question: How far ahead should I start?
items.answer: As early as possible. Interview wait times in Indian cities can run to many months at busy periods, and they are the single most common reason a US trip slips. We begin the moment a trip is on your horizon.

items.question: What if I'm refused?
items.answer: We reduce the risk by preparing an honest, consistent file and readying you for the interview: most refusals turn on doubt about intent rather than paperwork. The decision is the consular officer's alone, and no one can promise an outcome.
